title: Topological sort: Kahn's algorithm
summary: An order of courses 0..n-1 that respects every (before, after) prerequisite, or [] if there is a cycle. Start with the courses that have none; finishing one lowers each dependent's in-degree, and a dependent at 0 is ready. O(V + E).
code: # Take any course with no unmet prerequisites; leftovers sit on a cycle.
queue = deque(node for node in range(n) if indegree[node] == 0)
return order if len(order) == n else []
triggers: order tasks so every dependency comes first
decide whether dependencies contain a cycle
prompts: A build system knows which modules need which others compiled first. Produce a compile order, or report that none exists.
A recipe lists steps and which steps must finish before others can start. Find an order to do them all, or show that the recipe is impossible.
invariant: Every course in the queue or in order has all of its prerequisites earlier in order.
mantra: Start with no prerequisites; a course is ready when its in-degree hits 0.
pitfalls: Count every in-degree before seeding the queue.
Fewer than n courses in order means the rest sit on a cycle: return [].
Edges point from prerequisite to dependent; reversing them reverses the order.
Many valid orders can exist; check the edges rather than one expected list.

anchors.name: Alien Dictionary
anchors.trick: The first differing letters of adjacent words give the edges; then sort.

anchors.name: Parallel Courses
anchors.trick: Process the queue level by level; the number of levels is the number of semesters.

mutations.explanation: On a cycle it returns a partial order instead of [], hiding the courses that can never be taken.
Decrements the finished course instead of its dependent, so dependents never reach 0 and valid schedules come back empty.
